# Table

```tsx
import { compareSortValues, Table, TableActions, TableBody, TableCell, TableCellAccordion, TableCellActions, TableCellSelection, TableCellSkeleton, TableEmpty, TableHead, TableHeader, TableRow, TableRowAccordion, tableCellVariants } from "@lucasdost/design-system"
```

Serve para exibir dados estruturados em formato tabular, facilitando a leitura e a comparação de informações.

## Example

From the Storybook story; names like `args` or `label` are the story controls.

```tsx
renderTable(args)
```

## Figma notes

Mirrors the Figma Table, on a native <table>:
- Rows are 56px with a Border/Secondary line inside them, so the padding under a 40px button or input takes that 1px.
- .Table Title Cell is TableHead, .Table Cell is TableCell, and .Table Cell Selection, Accordion, Actions and Skeleton are their own components, with `title` for Title=True.
- Loading=True is `loading` on Table: every cell turns into its skeleton.
- `selectable` on Table adds the .Table Cell Selection column by itself, after the Accordion one, and the Table keeps the selection: each row only needs a `value`. Single is a Radio Button per row, Multiple a Checkbox, with the title one selecting all the rows that aren't disabled.
- Accordion=True is TableRowAccordion, Empty=True is TableEmpty.
- Table Row State: Hover fills the row with Background/Hover, over the body rows only, and Disabled is the whole row at 50%, with its cells unchanged.
- `actions` on Table adds the .Table Actions column by itself: each row gives its `actions` and the Table type picks how they show.
- Sorting lives in the Table: with sortable columns, exactly one always sorts it, the first one until another is pressed. Pressing it again flips between Ascending and Descending. TableBody reorders its rows by their `sortValues`, and rows without them stay put, for data sorted elsewhere.
- Fixed Columns=True is `fixedColumns` on Table, for the selection and actions columns, and `fixed` on the other cells: they stick to their side, and the last one on the left and the right one take the Figma Content Left and Content Right line and Shadow/Large.
- `overflowMethod` on Table sets what long text does in the text cells and titles: Line Break wraps it and the row grows, Truncate keeps one line with an ellipsis, and None keeps one line and widens the column.
- The horizontal scroll takes the Figma Scroll Bar colors.

## Props

Documented props only; every component also accepts the props of the element or Base UI part it renders (`className`, events, ARIA…).

`TableCellLayoutProps`:

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fixed?` | `TableFixed` | Figma Fixed Columns: sticks the cell to this side of the table. |
| `fixedOffset?` | `number` | How far from the left a fixed cell stops, past the fixed cells before it. |
| `width?` | `"fill" \| "hug" \| number` | Figma Width: `fill` shares the free space, `hug` follows the content and a number is a fixed width that doesn't shrink. Set it on the whole column. |

`TableSelectionProps`:

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `selectable?` | `boolean` | Adds the selection column to every row. |
| `selectionType?` | `"single" \| "multiple"` | Single is a Radio Button per row, Multiple a Checkbox. |
| `selectedRows?` | `string[]` | The `value` of the selected rows, controlled. |
| `defaultSelectedRows?` | `string[]` | The `value` of the selected rows, uncontrolled. |
| `selectionLabel?` | `string` | Accessible name of the title cell. |

`TableProps`:

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `loading?` | `boolean` | Figma Loading: every cell of the table turns into its skeleton. |
| `fixedColumns?` | `boolean` | Sticks the selection column to the left and the actions to the right. |
| `overflowMethod?` | `TableOverflowMethod` | What long text does: wrap, end in an ellipsis or widen its column. |
| `actions?` | `TableActionsType` | Figma .Table Actions Type: adds the actions column to every row. |
| `actionsLabel?` | `string` | Accessible name of the actions title cell. |
| `moreActionsLabel?` | `string` | Accessible name of the Hidden Actions button. |
| `sort?` | `TableSortState` | The column sorting the table, controlled. |
| `defaultSort?` | `TableSortState` | The column sorting the table at first, instead of the first sortable one. |

`TableRowProps`:

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `disabled?` | `boolean` | Figma State Disabled: the row at 50%, and nothing in it responds. |
| `value?` | `string` | Identifies the row in the selection of a `selectable` table. |
| `selectLabel?` | `string` | Accessible name of the row's selection control. |
| `actions?` | `TableAction[]` | What this row offers in the actions column of the Table. |
| `sortValues?` | `Record<string, string \| number>` | The value of this row in each column, by `sortKey`, for TableBody to sort. |

`TableCellBaseProps`:

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title?` | `boolean` | Renders the Title=True cell, in the header row. |

## Rules

- Import `Table` from `@lucasdost/design-system`. Do not rebuild it with plain HTML and Tailwind classes.
- Style it through its props and variants first. Use `className` only for layout (margin, width, grid placement), never to change its colors, typography or radius.
- Colors come from the S0L tokens; see [color](../foundations/color.md).
